business_overview: Incorporated 1989, Vishnu Chemicals manufactures and exports chromium chemicals and barium compounds, serving 12+ industries across 57 countries from its Hyderabad base. Seeded via untrusted X triage (@bastionresearch, bullish, medium conviction, 2026-09-13).

fundamentals_narrative: Vishnu Chemicals continues to show real above-industry export-led revenue growth (FY26 +11.3% YoY to Rs 1,609.7 Cr; Q1 FY27 re-accelerated to +24.9% YoY), and management is explicitly moving up the value curve — Blanc Fixe (specialty barium derivative) launch, a new DMSO specialty-chemical plant (Rs 205-240 Cr, Rs 68 Cr spent), backward integration into barium raw materials (Ramadas Minerals) and a South Africa chrome-ore mine, and a 50:50 JV with France's DCX Chrome for a 6,000 MTPA high-purity chromium metal plant in Visakhapatnam. But this pass's fresh-filings read independently confirms the prior flag: ROCE has declined every year from a FY22 peak of ~30% to ~16.4% in FY26 (5-yr average ~19%), driven by two years of elevated chrome-ore input costs plus capital employed growing ahead of the new capacity coming online. FY26 free cash flow was again negative (CFO ~Rs 127 Cr vs. capex well above that as CWIP built to Rs 159 Cr) as debt-funded capex continues (gross debt Rs 315 Cr -> Rs 527 Cr, FY24-26). Near-term margin is under fresh pressure too: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin dipped to 15.1% (from 16.1% Q1 FY26) on a one-off Rs 8 Cr retrospective barium charge, and management flagged ocean-freight costs rising to ~20% of revenue in Q2 FY27 on West Asia disruption — partially offset by chrome-ore prices now softening through 2026 on abundant South African supply. Promoter holding has stabilised at 69.21% for five straight quarters (no pledge) after declining ~5.8pp over the prior three years. Chromium/barium remain relatively commoditized product lines — barium in particular faces structural Chinese pricing pressure — so the specialty pivot (Blanc Fixe/DMSO/DCX) is the real but unproven differentiator; management's own target of 20% EBITDA margin by FY28 (from ~15.7% FY26) is the clearest test of whether the capex cycle pays off.
